official.deadline_note: No call is open as of 10 October 2026 - the HK-dir programme page shows 'Grants you can apply for now: 0'. The most recent call closed 3 June 2024 at 12:00 CEST, and the official 2024 call text states the next call for applications is foreseen in 2028, subject to approval by the Parliament.
official.application_cycle: 2024 call was the last published round; next call foreseen in 2028, subject to approval by the Parliament
official.status_note: The Norwegian government has proposed to end support for the NORPART-programme in the 2025 National Budget. Only seven projects received funding from the NOK 35 million allocated for 2024, and ongoing projects will receive funding in accordance with their agreements.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Exchange students in the NORPART programme will be exempted from paying tuition fees in Norway.
benefits: Exchange students in the NORPART programme will be exempted from paying tuition fees in Norway.
You may apply for up to NOK 5 million in funding per project.
The budget for the programme is NOK 35 million per year for the period 2024 to 2028, subject to annual approval by the Parliament.
There is no requirement for own contribution in the project budget.
Eligible costs include personnel and administration, procurement of services and equipment, Master's and PhD exchange costs, travel and accommodation costs, and other project-related costs.
eligibility: The applicant must be an accredited Norwegian higher education institution or a Norwegian institution with accredited higher education programs.

Each application must include at least one accredited higher education institution in a NORPART partner country; the partner-country list published by HK-dir currently includes Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda and 30 other countries, with South Africa limited to Historically Disadvantaged Institutions (HDIs).
Projects may target all academic fields at master and PhD level.
Full degrees at master and PhD level cannot be funded by the program, and student mobility at the Bachelor's level is not supported.
NORPART focuses on master's students, with some PhD activities possible; maximum long-term academic stays are 12 months at master level and 18 months at PhD level.
requirements: The application must be submitted by the deadline applicable to the call.
The application must be submitted through the HK-dir application portal (Espresso).
The application must be written in English.
The application must be submitted on behalf of an organisation that can be entered as applicant under this call.
The application must include at least one partner institution that is an accredited higher education institution in a NORPART partner country.
The application must meet the duration requirements that apply to the call.
documents: A signed version of HK-dir's declaration of participation from the person in the applicant organisation with legal responsibility for the application.
Letters of commitment from all project partners, excluding the applicant institution, documenting their interest in and commitment to the project by the leadership at the relevant level.
A curriculum vitae (CV) for the project coordinator at the applicant institution.
selection_criteria: Quality of project design and implementation (30%)
Quality of the project group and collaborative structures (20%)
To qualify for a grant, all final sub-grades must be higher than 2, and at least three out of four sub-grades must be 4 or higher.
application_method: Applications must be submitted through the HK-dir application portal Espresso.
Applications are considered by two people with special expertise, with a third assessor in case of disagreement, and final decisions on grants are made by HK-dir.
official.application_route: Institutional route only: an accredited Norwegian higher education institution applies through the Espresso portal, and students take part through a funded project at their home institution.
official.study_mode: Full-time exchange stays, with virtual and hybrid (blended) mobility also supported
official.citizenship_residency: No individual citizenship rule is published; mobility runs between Norway and accredited institutions in the listed NORPART partner countries, with South Africa restricted to HDIs.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme funds mobility of students from partner countries to Norway and of Norwegian students to partner countries, but only through institutional applications.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Projects may target all academic fields at master and PhD level; in South Africa, collaboration is limited to universities designated as Historically Disadvantaged Institutions (HDIs).
official.duration: Funded projects under the 2024 call had to start between 1 November and 31 December 2024 and end by 31 December 2028; individual exchange stays are capped at 12 months (master) and 18 months (PhD).
official.description: NORPART (Norwegian Partnership Programme for Global Academic Cooperation) supports long-term academic collaboration and mutual student mobility between higher education institutions in Norway and selected partner countries in the Global South. It is administered by the Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir) and funded by the Ministry of Education and Research and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
official.region: Norway (host country); partner countries across Africa, Asia and Latin America
official.program_type: Institutional project partnership grant with student and staff mobility
official.english_requirement: No individual English test requirement is published; the 2024 call requires that the application must be written in English.

All amounts, deadlines, eligibility rules, documents and assessment criteria were taken from HK-dir's own NORPART programme page and the official 2024 Call for Applications PDF; no aggregator figure was used.

applicant_utility.summary: NORPART is not an individual scholarship but an institutional collaboration grant that only an accredited Norwegian higher education institution can apply for, so a student can never submit an application directly. Students at partner-country universities join only through an existing funded project at their own institution, where they study as exchange students: tuition is waived in Norway and travel and accommodation are paid from the project budget, while any personal living stipend depends entirely on the individual project. Because the government proposed ending NORPART support in the 2025 National Budget, no round is currently open and HK-dir's own call text foresees the next one only in 2028, subject to Parliament.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled master's or PhD students whose home institution already runs a NORPART project with a Norwegian partner, and staff at Norwegian accredited institutions building Global South partnerships.
application_readiness_checklist: Contact your international office first and ask whether your institution holds a current NORPART project agreement with a Norwegian institution - without it there is no student route at all.
Confirm your home institution is accredited and located in one of the 40 listed NORPART partner countries, and that you are enrolled at master or PhD level (full degrees cannot be funded).
Ask for the internal nomination deadline, which always falls well before any HK-dir institutional deadline.
Check your degree will be issued by your home institution or as a joint degree, as NORPART requires this.
Plan an exchange of at most 12 months (master) or 18 months (PhD) and budget for insurance, visa and living costs yourself.
common_rejection_risks: Submitting an individual student application - only institutions are eligible applicants, so such applications cannot even be registered.
Expecting NORPART to fund a full master's or PhD degree, which the official call explicitly excludes.
Assuming a listed partner country guarantees an exchange place: nationally only seven projects were funded in the last round, so a spot exists only if your institution is in one of them.

Project-style applications failing on formalities: missing letters of commitment, missing signed declaration of participation, an application not written in English, or a budget with no activity in at least one project year.

Weak assessment performance on the weighted criteria - relevance (30%), project design (30%), project group (20%) and impact (20%) - where all sub-grades must exceed 2 and three of four must be 4 or higher.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: No per-student stipend, insurance or living-allowance figure is published: mobility money comes from the project budget's exchange, travel and accommodation cost lines, so students must fund their own subsistence, visas, insurance and any costs beyond the project's budgeted rates.
document_audit: Letters of commitment must come from leadership at the relevant level at every partner institution except the applicant - unsigned or loosely worded letters sink applications.
The signed declaration of participation must be from the person with legal responsibility in the applicant organisation, not the project coordinator.
The application must be written in English, and attachments beyond the required list are not assessed at all.
A CV of the project coordinator at the applicant institution is a mandatory attachment.
alerts: Do not trust the '15 October 2026' deadline circulating on scholarship aggregator sites: HK-dir's own pages show no open call, and the last institutional deadline was 3 June 2024.
The 2025 National Budget proposes ending NORPART support; ongoing projects continue only under their existing agreements, so mobility availability shrinks each year until the next call.
Nigeria is not on HK-dir's current NORPART partner-country list, and South African participation is restricted to eight named Historically Disadvantaged Institutions.
Bangladesh is on the current partner-country list, contradicting catalogue notes that question its eligibility.
The next call is foreseen in 2028 only, subject to approval by the Norwegian Parliament.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: A Norwegian institution prepares and submits the application in the Espresso portal before the call deadline (12:00 CEST), HK-dir has two experts assess and grade it and decides awards by ranking, and students are then nominated into the funded project by their home institution.
